*J U D G M E N T*

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/, on account of the injuries sustained by her, in a road traffic accident.

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*
2. Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on 5.9.2016, at about 6.30 p.m., the petitioner was travelling in a Maruti D'zire car bearing registration No.KA04 MG Smt.Deepa vs Shri Srinivasa N.S on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192556377/
1 1343 along with other inmates.

It is alleged that, the said car was driving by one Srinivas  respondent No.1, on Bengaluru  Mangaluru NH75 road, and when they reached near Shark Dhabha, Kuduru Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara District, he was driving the said car, with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the rear side of the lorry, which was proceeding ahead of the said car.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated in the petition that, immediately, the petitioner was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru wherein, first aid treatment was taken, then she was shifted to Sakra hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein, she was admitted as an inpatient.

It is stated that, the petitioner had incurred Rs.1,00,000/ towards hospitalization, conveyance, medical treatment and other incidental charges etc.
4.

It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 28 years, doing tailoring and saree business and used to earn a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, she has suffered mental shock and agony, and she could not work as she was earlier to the accident.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Maruthi D'zire Car bearing registration No.KA04MG1343.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Kudur police as per Crime No.278/2016 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
6. After service of the notice of this petition, though the respondent No.1 has appeared before the court through his counsel, not filed written statement, in answer to the case of the petitioner.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 made appearance before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement, in answer to the case of the petitioner.
7. The respondent No.2, in the written statement, has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

But, strongly denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and admitted about the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending Maruthi Swift D'zire Car bearing registration No.KA05MG 1343, in favour of the respondent No.1, as on the date of the accident, subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
It is the contention of the respondent that, two vehicles were involved in the alleged accident, and there was a contributory negligence.
However, owner and insurer of the Lorry bearing registration No.TN04AP6692 are not made as parties.
As such, the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
It is stated that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid DL, as on the date of the accident and also the driver of said lorry not holding valid DL, at the time of accident.
And there was no valid permit and fitness certificate, consequently, there is violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
As such, the respondent company is not liable to pay any compensation.
And the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against their company.

Smt.Deepa vs Shri Srinivasa N.S on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192556377/
2 8.

On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of this case,
following issues were framed:
*ISSUES*
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing registration NO.KA05MG 1343 on 5.9.2016 at about 6.30 p.m., near Shark Daba, on NH75 road, Kuduru Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, by name Smt.Deepa.D during the course of evidence, placed her affidavit evidence, in lieu of examinationinchief, who examined as PW1 in the case on hand.
At the time of her evidence, 10 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
In addition to her evidence, placed the evidence of the Dr.Ananda Reddy.
as PW2.
At the time of his evidence placed five documents marked as Ex.P11 to Ex.P15, for consideration.
10. On the other hand, to prove the defenses forthcoming in the objection, the respondents have not adduced any rebuttal evidence for consideration.
Hence, the matter was set down for arguments.
11. Heard the argument of both the counsel.
Perused the materials available on record.
At the time of argument, learned counsel for the petitioner and the respondent No.2 have filed the written arguments.
I have gone through the same.

12. On appreciation of the evidence available on record, my findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order For the following:
*R E A S O N S* ISSUE NO.1:
13.

It is the case of the petitioner Smt.Deepa.D that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, Maruthi Swift D'zire Car bearing registration No.KA04MG 1343, alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

On the other hand, respondent No.1 being the owner cum driver of the offending vehicle, and husband of the petitioner, remained as silent spectator without challenging the case of the petitioner by filing written statement and adducing evidence.

The respondent No.2, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously dispute the allegation of the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, and strongly contended that,
Smt.Deepa vs Shri Srinivasa N.S on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192556377/
3 there is a contributory negligence, and violation of the terms and conditions of the policy, as well as the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
14.

On the basis of the rival contentions of both the parties, it is pertinent to note that, as per section 101 of the evidence Act, and section 166 of M.V Act, burden is on the petitioner, to prove the above issue, on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
To discharge the burden lies on the petitioner Deepa D, placed her affidavit evidence by reiterating the main petition averments.
Among the documentary evidence Ex.P1 to Ex.P6 are the material documents in connection with the above issue.
And remaining documents along with the evidence of PW2 are to be discussed in detail at the time of discussion of issue No.2.
On the other hand, the respondents herein, in connection with the stand of the petitioner, and the evidence given by her, have not adduced any rebuttal evidence for consideration.
In such a situation, duty is more on the part of the court, to assess the evidence available on record, in order to come to the proper conclusion with respect to the above issue.
15. In the affidavit evidence of PW1, reiterated the main petition averments.
On taking birds eye view towards the documents placed by the petitioner, to demonstrate her stand, reveal that, on 05.09.2016 accident in question had taken place.
In this regard, first information was given on 06.09.2016 by one M.Shekar, who is none other than the driver of the defending vehicle Lorry.

In connection with one day delay in giving first information is concerned, in the recitals of the complaint, and in column No.3(c) of the Ex.P.1, he stated that, after giving information about the accident, to his owner, he gave belated complaint.
In connection with this reasons, no rebuttal evidence available from the side of the respondents to disbelieve the said reason.
Hence, the point of two days delay is not fatal in the case on hand.

16. Added to this, it is pertinent to discuss that, on the basis of first information given by the complainant, criminal law set in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle Car bearing registration No.KA05MG1343 alleging that, he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.

In the recitals of the complaint and in column No.10 of the Ex.P1, there is a clear narration with respect to the negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle on the fateful of the accident, which caused injuries to the petitioner.

The recitals of the Ex.P1 &
Ex.P2 complaint
remained unquestioned by the other side to prove the innocence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

It is relevant to discuss herein that, in the written statement of the respondent No.2, had taken several defenses about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, and also, had taken the defence of contributory negligence and about the plea of non joinder of necessary parties.

But, to prove the innocence of the driver of the offending vehicle, the driver cum owner of the said vehicle, neither made an effort to question the recitals of the Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 well in time,
before the competent court of law, nor placed counter complaint, to prove the innocence of the driver of the offending vehicle, and also to show that, there was a contributory negligence.

17. Apart from this, the mahazar process conducted by the investigation officer, in the presence of complainant and punch witness reflect about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, and the said recitals indicates towards the guilt of the driver of the offending vehicle, and no whisper about the contributory negligence in the said document.

In addition to this, the damages Smt.Deepa vs Shri Srinivasa N.S on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192556377/
4 noted in the report of the motor vehicle inspector as per Ex.P.4, pertaining to the offending and defending vehicles, clearly speak about the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Since, as per the report, accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles, involved in the accident, and in the accident, front portion of the car was damaged, and rear right side of the defending vehicle was damaged.
Another material document, Ex.P6 wound certificate speaks that, on the history of RTA, the petitioner had sustained 2 grievous injuries and 2 simple injuries.
All these material documents remained unshaken.

18. Ultimately, on going through the final report submitted by the investigation officer, as per Ex.P5 reflects that, after due investigation process final report has been submitted against the driver of the offending vehicle by name Srinivas N.S, who is the driver cum owner of the offending vehicle, on the allegation fully made in the column No.17 of the charge sheet and also alleged that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

Another material point is necessary to note herein that, the driver of the offending vehicle was none other than the husband of the petitioner, and tortfeasor in connection with the accident in question.

The final report submitted by the investigation officer, though not substantive piece of documents to consider the claim petition, not strongly denied by the other side to prove the innocence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
As such, there is no hurdle to taken in to consideration the police papers in proof of the above issue in the absence of contra documents from the side of the respondents.
19. At the time of crossexamination of PW1, admitted that, as on the date of the accident, her husband was driving the motor cycle.

And contrary to her pleadings stated that, accident in question was taken place, due to the mistake on the part of the driver of the lorry, consequently, herself along with her husband and son, sustained injuries.
And her husband has not filed any claim petition.
And denied the suggestion that, since, on their mistake accident in question had taken place, belated complaint was given.
Except this point, no other material points culled out, to prove all the defences forthcoming in the written statement of the respondent company.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 being the tortfeasor, not made an effort to cross examine the PW1, to prove his innocence, and to prove the guilt on the part of the driver of the defending vehicle.

Though some of the minor contradictions could be seen, on appreciation of the entire evidence of the PW1, on evaluation of the evidence of the PW1 in toto, along with the documentary evidence, it is crystal clear that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car, accident in question had taken place.
Added to this, MLC extract and Police intimation placed by the PW2, as per Ex.P.13 and Ex.P.14 are also, substantiate the case of the petitioner.
To rebut the same, no evidence available on record, from the side of the respondents.
Hence, the evidence of the petitioner has to be accepted.

20. In the light of the evidence placed on record, by the petitioner, in the case on hand, by way of affidavit and the documentary evidence, I am of the view that, the petitioner has placed satisfactory evidence, to prove the above issue to the effect that, the alleged accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Maruthi Swift D'zire Car bearing registration No.KA 04 MG1343.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the Issue No.1, in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
Smt.Deepa vs Shri Srinivasa N.S on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192556377/
5 21.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident, under different heads.

22. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by her,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.

Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.

entities.text: Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.

The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."
23.

In the light of the preposition laid down in the above case, it is also relevant to note that, "while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.

"
24. In connection with the injuries sustained by the petitioner, in the accident, has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P6.

The said document discloses that, he sustained the following injuries:
1. Sutured lacerated wound over left upper eyelid and periorbital region.
2. Diffuse odema present over dorsum of nose, no bony injuries.
3. CT scan of brain and xray of chest and cervical spine shows no bony injuries.
4. Sutured wound over left lower eye lid with loss of tissue.
25.
According to the doctor, injuries No.1 and are simple in nature.
Apart from this, the petitioner has produced, discharge summary, medical bill & prescription marked as per Ex.P7 to Ex.P9.
In addition to her evidence, got examined Dr.Ananda Reddy.
as PW2 and placed inpatient file, MLC extract, Police intimation and CT scan film Ex.P12 to Ex.P15, for consideration.
As per the discharge summary of Sakra hospital, Bengaluru marked at Ex.P7, the petitioner had taken treatment as an inpatient from 6.9.2016 to 10.9.2016 i.e. for a period of five days.

For having taken the note of the nature of the injuries sustained by her, and by keeping in mind about her sufferings during the said period of treatment, in connection with the grievous injuries, and by considering the mode of treatment given to the petitioner, in the hospital, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for Smt.Deepa vs Shri Srinivasa N.S on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192556377/
6 compensation of Rs.40,000/ towards pain and suffering.
26.
Another point to be discussed herein, about the loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
In the petition, she has stated that, she was doing Tailoring and Saree business and getting an income of Rs.25,000/ per month.
To substantiate this, she has not placed any iota of documents to show the income of Rs.25,000/ per month.
On the other hand, it is to be noted that, the injuries sustained by her are both grievous and simple in nature, as per the wound certificate.

On going through the discharge summary of Sakra hospital, Bengaluru marked at Ex.P7, the petitioner had taken treatment as an inpatient from 6.9.2016 to 10.9.2016 Hence, definitely, there was some difficulty to her, during the period of treatment, to do daily routine work and to do her work for livelihood at least for one month.
At the time of treatment to the injuries fully mentioned in the wound certificate, she could have suffered a lot and faced difficulty to do her work.
Hence, I am of the view that, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,500/ towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

27. The petitioner herein, in connection with her treatment expenses, at the time of her evidence,
placed entire medical bill of Rs.2,230/ as per Ex.P8 along with prescription as per Ex.P9.

Though some questions put to this witness at the time of crossexamination of PW1 with respect to the medical bills, nothing has been elicited to disprove the contents of Ex.P.8, to the effect that, the said bills are created for the purpose of the case, same has been denied by the PW1.
On going through the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, and meager medical bills, in the absence of the contra materials, the said bills are apt to be accepted.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs. 2,230/ under the head of medical expenses.
28. The petitioner herein, as per the medical records, had sustained two grievous injuries and two simple injuries, fully mentioned in the wound certificate.
As per the evidence of the petitioner, she took treatment in Sakra hospital and later discharged with the advice of followup treatment.
As such, during the period of treatment, she could have spent some amount towards travelling, food and nourishment and for attendant.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,000/ towards attendant charges, food, and nourishment and conveyance charges.
29. Another material point of loss of future income is concerned, the petitioner herein, asserting that, she has sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by her.

In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on her evidence along with the wound certificate,
along with other medical documents.
In the evidence of the PW1, reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition, as per Ex.P6.

To substantiate this, the petitioner has placed,
wound certificate and discharge summary for consideration.
Added to this, placed the evidence of Dr. Ananda Reddy as PW2, to prove the disability sustained by the petitioner, consequent upon the accident.
30. In the evidence of PW2, deposed that, on the history of RTA the petitioner had been to Sakra World Hospital.

On diagnosis found, " 1. Sutured lacerated wound over left upper eyelid and periorbital region, 2. Diffuse edema present over dorsum of nose and no bony injuries. 3. Sutured wound over left lower eyelid with loss of tissue."

In this regard, she was admitted to Sakra World Smt.Deepa vs Shri Srinivasa N.S on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192556377/
7 Hospital on 6 th September under plastic surgery department to manage, multiple facial injuries.

entities.text: Sakra World Smt.Deepa vs Shri Srinivasa N.S
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On taking scan, shown multiple bony fragments in the soft tissue of the left orbitofrontal region.
And there was a comminuted depressed fracture of the anterior wall of the left frontal sinus with associated hemosinus.
Further, on taking xray of nasal bone, with C.T scan, of brain and face, as well as chest, and on routine laboratory investigation, treated to her by the team of doctors.
On 7th September 2016, debridement and suturing of facial injuries were done, after the removal of suturing of facial injuries and after removal of necrosed tissue under general anesthesia.

Thereafter,
she was discharged from the hospital with proper recommendations and advice to follow up.
Except this, and production of te documents Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.15, this witness has not spoken about the percentage of disability sustained by the petitioner, consequent upon the accidental injuries.
31. At the time of crossexamination of PW2 admitted about issuance of wound certificate.
stated that, he issued wound certificate.
And answers given by this witness, spakes that, he gave first aid treatment to the petitioner.

Subsequently, for plastic surgery she approached the PW2, and as per his evidence, team of doctors gave treatment to her, and she took treatment in the mode fully mentioned in page No.3 para No.6 of the examination in chief evidence of PW2.
But, no whisper about the percentage of disability sustained by the petitioner on evaluation of the evidence of the PW2 in toto.
But, it is crystal clear that, due to the accident, she sustained facial injuries.
In this regard, she took treatment for 5 days.
No document about the follow up treatment.

No evidence to show how the injuries sustained by the petitioner, losses her future income, when the doctor has not expressed his opinion about the physical disability, then it is difficult to assess the functional disability.

On going through the injury of the petitioner caused on the face, and the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate, and the systematic examination report forthcoming in the Ex.P.7, it is relevant to note that, due to the accident, some scar marks could be in the face of the petitioner.
Further, it is forthcoming in the Ex.P.7, consequent upon the accident, there was a loss of tissue in the lower eyelid, loss of eyelid, loss of eyebrow left side.

By taking in to consideration of all these aspects, and due to the facial injuries, some scar marks could be in the face of the petitioner,
along with the said scar she has to live and she has not produced any document, to show her condition, after the discharge from the hospital and consequently upon the follow up treatment.
Hence, I am of the view that, the petitioner herein, is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.
But with respect to the facial disfigurement it is apt to grant compensation of Rs.30,000/ towards facial disfigurement.
Same will meet the ends of justice.

32. Next factual aspect loss of amenities is concerned, on going through the evidence of PW1 and PW2, and on appreciation of the entire medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,000/ towards loss of amenities.
33. In connection with the future medication expenses is concerned, the PW2 at the time of his evidence, has not stated about the future medication.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of future medication.

34. In view of my due discussions held above, on various aspects, the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation Smt.Deepa vs Shri Srinivasa N.S on 20 February, 2023

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192556377/
8  amount  1. Pain and Suffering Rs.40,00000 2. Loss of income during Rs. 9,50000 laidup period and rest period 3.

Medical expenses Rs. 2,23000 4.Attendant, Rs. 5,00000 Nourishment and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Nil 6. Compensation Rs. 30,00000 towards facial disfigurement 7. Loss of Amenities Rs. 3,00000
8.Future medication Nil

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.89,730/ (Rupees eighty nine thousand seven hundred and thirty only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016,
Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated.
20.03.2018.

entities.text: Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.

LIABILITY:
36.

In so far as, liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, accident in question had taken place.

As such, the respondent No.1 being the R.C owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
37. On the other hand, the respondent No.2, in the case on hand, has not seriously disputed the existence of the insurance policy, as on the date of the accident.
And no evidence is available on record, to show that, there is a violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, by its owner.
Further, no rebuttal evidence from the side of the respondents, to disprove the case of the petitioner.
38. As per the records, the policy was in force from 29.10.2015 to 28.10.2016.
Alleged accident had taken place on 5.9.2016.
As such, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners, as per the order of this court.

However, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company has to indemnify the loss of the respondent No.1, towards the payment of award amount, to the petitioner, who is the third party in the case on hand.
Resultantly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

Smt.Deepa vs Shri Srinivasa N.S on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192556377/
9 ISSUE NO.3:
39.

In view of my due discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
*O R D E R* The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.89,730/ (Rupees eighty nine thousand seven hundred and thirty only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2insurance company is liable to pay the compensation determined by this court, with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the award amount with interest, since the compensation amount is meager, the entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.decision:
34. In view of my due discussions held above, on various aspects, the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation Smt.Deepa vs Shri Srinivasa N.S on 20 February, 2023
Medical expenses Rs. 2,23000 4.Attendant, Rs. 5,00000 Nourishment and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Nil 6. Compensation Rs. 30,00000 towards facial disfigurement 7. Loss of Amenities Rs. 3,00000
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.89,730/ (Rupees eighty nine thousand seven hundred and thirty only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016,
Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated.
20.03.2018.
38. As per the records, the policy was in force from 29.10.2015 to 28.10.2016.
Alleged accident had taken place on 5.9.2016.
As such, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners, as per the order of this court.
However, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company has to indemnify the loss of the respondent No.1, towards the payment of award amount, to the petitioner, who is the third party in the case on hand.
Resultantly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
In view of my due discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
*O R D E R* The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.89,730/ (Rupees eighty nine thousand seven hundred and thirty only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2insurance company is liable to pay the compensation determined by this court, with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the award amount with interest, since the compensation amount is meager, the entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/.
Draw award accordingly.
